name: HAYSTAC
full_name: Haloscope At Yale Sensitive To Axion CDM
summary: HAYSTAC is a high-frequency cryogenic-cavity axion search, initially named ADMX-HF, that developed squeezed-state receivers.
detection_principle: A magnetized cavity converts axions to microwaves; squeezed-vacuum readout lowers effective quantum noise to improve scanning speed.

phases.name: RAY
phases.description: Rydberg Atoms at Yale, a subsequent approach using Rydberg-atom single-photon readout.

results.summary: Phase II excludes couplings in particular mass intervals and validates the scanning-rate improvement from quantum squeezing.

science_scope: Directly searches for Galactic-halo axions, axionlike particles or other ultralight dark matter. Limits depend on assumed local density, velocity distribution and coupling models; separate scanned mass intervals do not amount to exclusion of the entire range.
